newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier has 19 pct profit growth target.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier has 19 pct profit growth target.

text.p: Bombardier Inc said on Thursday that its business targets include an annual net profit growth rate of 19 percent compounded and a pre-tax profit margin of 9 percent.

"We have set another ambitious objective to reach an aggregate pre-tax profit margin of 9 percent for our operations," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Laurent Beaudoin told the aerospace and transportation equipment maker's annual meeting.
Bombardier's pre-tax profit margin was 7.6 percent in fiscal 1997 ended January 31 versus 6.6 percent in 1996.

Bombardier's net income increased 30 percent in fiscal 1997 to C$406 million or C$ 1.18 a share from C$313 million or C$0.92 a share a year earlier, excluding a writedown of C$155 million or C$0.47 a share on its investment in Eurotunnel share units in fiscal 1996.

Beaudoin said the company plans to double its sales in five years, and by boosting the pre-tax profit margin to 9 percent, expects to "maintain earnings growth at a compounded annual rate of 19 percent for the next five years."
Beaudoin said he expects the company to achieve its business objectives by introducing a number of new products.

Those include the launch of its new Learjet 45 business jet this year, and its Global Express long-range business jet next year, as well as the introduction of the Dash 8 Series 400 turboprop plane in 1996 and the 70-seat Canadair Regional Jet Series 700 in 2000.
Beaudoin said Bombardier produced 168 planes last year and expects to make about 200 this year.

With the opening of its aircraft completion center in Dorval, Quebec this December, Bombardier will also begin completing the interiors for the Challenger 604 and Global Express business jets, he said.

Aside from avoiding having to pay subcontractors for aircraft completion, the new center will also allow Bombardier to maintain tighter quality control of interior finishing for those aircraft, he said.

Beaudoin told reporters after the meeting that most of the company's growth will be generated internally, but he did not exclude the possibility of making acquisitions in sectors in which the company already operates.
Beaudoin reiterated his concerns over the company's loss on June 17 of a US$1.0 billion jet order to Brazilian state-owned plane maker Embraer.

While Bombardier picked up a US$1.4 billion order from AMR Corp 's American Eagle Airlines for 25 of its 70-seat Canadair Regional Jets, with options for 25 more, Embraer won American Eagle's order for 42 of its 50-seat jets, plus options for 25 more.
Beaudoin said Bombardier has asked the Canadian government to lodge a complaint with the World Trade Organization regarding Brazil's "illegal" direct subsidies to Embraer and its customers.

Beaudoin said Embraer offered American Eagle a direct subsidy of US$2.3 million for each plane ordered. Those subsidies significantly reduced the roughly US$15 million list price for each Embraer jet ordered by American Eagle, he said.
"It is the kind of subsidy that in my view makes the market forces totally uncompetitive," Beaudoin said.
Bombardier's 50-seat Regional Jet has a retail sticker prices of about US$20 million.
